understanding.purpose: Compare income statement line items across fiscal 2024 quarters and against the full-year total, in USD millions.
understanding.reading: Readers scan row labels to find a line item, then read across to compare quarters and the full year; they can also scan down a quarter to compare line items. The long cost-of-revenue label will create a taller row that can absorb its own wrapping.
groups: Columns 2–5 are equivalent quarterly measures and benefit from similar widths.
Column 6 is another monetary measure but represents the full year; its distinct header needs more space if it is to stay on one line.
Column 1 identifies each row and needs most of the flexible text space.
keep_intact: Individual words in row labels and headers
may_wrap: The long cost-of-revenue label at word boundaries
Research and development at word boundaries
Full year between its two words
USD millions between its two words

preferred.name: r1A
preferred.note: Keep Full year on one line while using the narrower quarter widths from r0A and r0C. This returns 4px to the label column compared with r0B and tests whether the long label can wrap more compactly without splitting words or values.

preferred.name: r3A
preferred.note: Give Full year the 89px it needs to stay on one line, taking 14px from the label column. This makes the header hierarchy cleaner while preserving enough width for all numeric values and individual words; check whether the narrower labels create an undesirable extra line.

acceptable.name: r0A
acceptable.note: Give the row labels the most space while keeping every numeric value intact, allowing Full year to wrap.

acceptable.name: r0B
acceptable.note: Use equal quarter widths and keep Full year on one line, accepting more wrapping in row labels.

acceptable.name: r0C
acceptable.note: Split the flexible space between row labels and the full-year column, allowing its header to wrap while giving it more breathing room.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Move 14px from the full-year column to the row-label column. This keeps the full-year values intact while allowing its header to wrap between words, and tests whether the extra label space improves the line breaks.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Make all four quarterly columns 66px wide for a more regular comparison rhythm, taking 4px from the label column. Keep the compact full-year column and its two-line header.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The narrow quarter columns leave only 29px for text, forcing values and headers to break or overflow. The extra label width comes at the expense of comparing the figures.
bad.why: The narrow quarter columns leave only 29px for text, forcing values and headers to break or overflow. The extra label width comes at the expense of comparing the figures.

rationale: r1A and r3A are identical: they keep the quarter columns closely matched and the full-year heading on one line. The long expense label takes three lines, but its words stay intact and the figures remain easy to scan across the row. r0B preserves the single-line heading too, but its narrower label column adds a fourth line without a corresponding gain in the numeric columns.

general: Columns serving the same role benefit from similar widths, provided each has room for its contents.
Judge wrapping by its effect on reading and comparison, not by table height alone.
Preserve enough room for numeric values and identifiers before giving surplus width to labels.
specific: The full-year column needs 89px to fit its heading on one line with the stated padding.
The expense label is the main constraint on row height; a modest reduction in its column width adds a line in r0B.

tradeoffs: A designer could prefer r0A or r2A for the slightly wider label column, accepting a two-line full-year heading. r0B gives the year total more space but makes the longest row taller.
uncertain: The ranges are narrow, approximate design tolerances, not browser-tested boundaries. They describe individual adjustments with the remaining widths redistributed proportionally within the 552px limit; quarter columns must retain enough room for their values.

critique.good: The wider label column keeps the long cost-of-revenue label to three lines and gives the table a compact, readable rhythm. Quarterly values remain intact and align in comparable columns.
critique.problems: The Full year header wraps, making the annual measure slightly less immediate to identify.
critique.cause: The 75px full-year column has 54px of text space, short of the 68px needed for its header on one line.

critique.good: Full year stays on one line, and the four equally sized quarter columns reinforce their equivalent roles. All values remain intact.
critique.problems: The cost-of-revenue label takes four lines, creating a conspicuously tall row with much empty space beneath the numbers.
critique.cause: The 89px full-year column and four 66px quarter columns leave 199px for row labels, too little to retain the more compact wrapping seen in the other designs.

critique.good: The long label stays on three lines, values remain intact, and the quarters form a balanced group. The full-year column has more breathing room than in r0A.
critique.problems: Full year still wraps, so the extra width does not resolve the header break; the label column is also narrower than in r0A without reducing the table height.
critique.cause: At 82px, the full-year column provides 61px of text space, still below the 68px needed for the complete header.

critique.good: The four quarters form a consistent group, and the full-year column is clearly distinguished. All values, quarter identifiers and words remain intact. The long cost-of-revenue label wraps naturally, and each row remains easy to follow across.
critique.problems: The first column is relatively narrow, so the cost-of-revenue label takes three lines and Research and development takes two. The full-year column has enough room for its header on one line, but that space comes at the expense of the row labels.
critique.cause: At 203px, the first column has 182px for text. The 89px full-year column reserves 68px for its one-line header; the quarterly columns are already at their minimum widths for the values.

critique.good: The row labels form a clear left-hand anchor, and the quarterly columns make a compact, coherent group under Fiscal 2024. Numeric values and individual words remain intact. The long cost-of-revenue label wraps naturally, while the short rows stay compact.
critique.problems: The Full year header wraps, making the two-level header feel uneven. Research and development also wraps, adding height to an otherwise short row.
critique.cause: The full-year column is 75px wide, leaving 54px for a header that needs 68px on one line. The 217px label column leaves 196px for text, so longer labels wrap.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

ref_equal.why: The row-header column is so narrow that several words break apart, making labels hard to read and producing very tall rows.

r0B.why: Numbers and headers stay intact, and the quarters form a clear group. The long cost label wraps to four lines, giving that row extra height.

ref_auto.why: The labels wrap at word boundaries and all figures remain intact. The narrow full-year column forces its header onto two lines.

r1A.why: Row labels wrap naturally, the figures remain intact, and the quarter columns have a consistent rhythm. Full year also fits on one line.

contrast.why: The quarter columns are too narrow, splitting nearly every figure across lines and making comparisons unreliable.

r0A.why: Labels and figures remain intact, with balanced quarter columns. The full-year header wraps to two lines despite fitting on one line in D.

r0B.why: Quarter columns are balanced, numbers stay intact, and Full year fits on one line. The narrow label column makes the longest row unnecessarily tall.

ref_equal.why: The label column is so narrow that words split across lines, making row names difficult to read and creating excessive row heights.

r0A.why: Row labels wrap at word boundaries, numbers remain intact, and the quarter columns have a consistent rhythm. Full year wraps onto two lines.

ref_auto.why: Labels and numbers remain readable, with balanced quarter columns. Full year wraps onto two lines, and the numeric columns are fairly tight.

r1A.why: The labels wrap cleanly, all numbers stay intact, and Full year fits on one line. The four quarter columns are balanced and the rows scan well.

contrast.why: The numeric columns are too narrow, splitting many figures across lines and making comparisons unreliable.

raw.unsure: C and D are very close visually; their small differences in column proportions have little effect on readability.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
